note: inferred: departs Deptford in the Charles (King's pinnace, 70-80 tons, 20 men and 2 boys), two days before James sails from Bristol
inferred: enters Hudson's Strait, sailing close along the north shore
inferred: reaches Salisbury Island, beset by ice
inferred: passes Cary's Swan's Nest, turns north-west (Cary's Swan's Nest placed at 63.9N 85.6W, near Cape Fullerton; the identification is Christy's and is not certain)
reaches an island off Cape Fullerton which he names Sir Thomas Roe's Welcome, then turns south down the west shore of the bay
inferred: in Churchill Bay, which he calls Hubart's Hope
inferred: enters Port Nelson to overhaul the ship; finds relics of Button's 1612-13 wintering, including an inscribed board
inferred: declares in his journal that all hope of a passage on this shore is at an end
inferred: meets Captain James's Henrietta Maria; visits exchanged, Foxe declines to winter with him
reaches and names Cape Henrietta Maria (Wolstenholme's Ultimum Vale), joining his discoveries to Hudson's
reaches his most northerly point, lat. 66 deg 47' N, long. 76 deg 55' W, named Foxe's Farthest; turns south on account of sickness among his crew
inferred: homeward through Hudson Strait; 'we are all in weak case'
inferred: passes Cape Chidleigh, clear of the ice, into the open ocean
arrives in the Downs with all his men alive and recovered, having lost not one man nor boy
